# @ternent/armour

> age encryption and identity decryption capabilities. No init or WASM step.

Stable interface: `npm install @ternent/armour@0.3.0 @ternent/identity@0.6.0`.
[Public README](https://github.com/ternent/core/blob/main/packages/armour/README.md).
Installed declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`. Imports use the package root.

## Capability encryption

```ts
import { generateIdentity, encryptAge } from "@ternent/armour";
import { ageRecipientFromPublicIdentity } from "@ternent/identity";
const created = await generateIdentity();
if (!created.ok) throw new Error(created.error.code);
const identity = created.value;
const recipient = ageRecipientFromPublicIdentity(identity.publicIdentity);
if (!recipient.ok) throw new Error(recipient.error.code);
const encrypted = await encryptAge({
  recipients: [recipient.value],
  plaintext: new TextEncoder().encode("hello"),
});
if (!encrypted.ok) throw new Error(encrypted.error.code);
const decrypted = await identity.decryptAge(encrypted.value);
if (!decrypted.ok) throw new Error(decrypted.error.code);
```

`generateIdentity()` and `identityFromSeed(seed)` return structured results containing
`IdentityCapability`: publicIdentity, exact-byte sign and decryptAge. A
`ReaderCapability` has publicIdentity and decryptAge only. `withAgeDecryption(base)`
synchronously wraps an Identity base capability. Private material remains host-owned.
`encryptAge({ recipients, plaintext })` returns a structured result containing binary
age bytes, accepts empty plaintext and encrypts with fresh material each time.
`decryptAgeWithSecret({ secret, ciphertext })` uses a raw 32-byte X25519 scalar.

## Convenience functions

`encryptForIdentities`, `encryptForRecipients`, `decryptWithIdentity` and
`decryptWithSecretKey` work with serialized identities/age strings and bytes.
`encryptWithPassphrase`/`decryptWithPassphrase`, text and binary variants are listed
in the README. Convenience encryption defaults to ASCII armor; select
`output: "binary"` where supported. Text decryptors return strings; byte/binary
helpers return bytes. Convenience helpers require nonempty data with a 64 MiB limit
and reject with ArmourError subclasses carrying codes; they do not return PrimitiveResult.
No `initArmour` call exists.

## Optional Ledger payload codec

`createAgeCodec({ recipients?, reader? })` returns an explicit byte codec with id age.
Recipients enable encode; reader enables decode. Supplying both guarantees both
methods in its type. Compose it with Ledger's `encodePayload`/`decodePayload`; Armour
never imports Ledger or manages its commits. A missing operation does not fall back
to plaintext. Decoder authentication/decryption failures return null (Ledger reports
locked); unexpected reader errors propagate. Signing, authorization, membership,
document history and storage are owned by other layers.
